note: Ceilings for tests/test_contract_agent.py: tool_calls counts every MCP tool call the two scripted seats make in one run, bytes_received the UTF-8 bytes of the text content of every answer. Both are the measured values, identical over five runs, with no headroom. Raise either only with a stated reason in the same PR. F2 lowered bytes_received by 616 (from 147,207): the desk's ready-lane and not_offered meanings were shortened when they gained the review-request answer. C6 raised bytes_received by 312 (from 146,591) with the same 56 calls: each my_desk answer's office carries `fence` with the comparison basis only, +324 over 6 desk reads; the work context's how_to_claim text is shorter, -12 over 2 reads. F12 lowered bytes_received by 37,423 (25.5%, from 146,903) with the same 56 calls: every answer's text is sent as compact JSON instead of indented JSON. The whitespace removed is 44,315 bytes; the seat's my_desk reads, which the budget cut, now carry more of the desk within the same budget (+6,892 bytes as dd594b1 would have rendered them). W3 raised bytes_received with the same 56 calls: each work-context answer carries the work_order report. F8 raised bytes_received by 1,031 (from 109,686) with the same 56 calls: the lease events the two seats drain carry their generation, handoff token and verdict as fields. A12 lowered tool_calls by 1 (56 to 55) and bytes_received by 39: the seat renews on the generation alone, so it no longer re-reads the issue for an ETag; the renewal hint is longer and claim answers carry issue_etag. F11 kept tool_calls at 55 and lowered bytes_received by 1,368: a claim_held refusal is followed by one quiet wait from its events_after cursor and then claim_next_ready, where it was followed by a lease read; the holder's lease_generation_required names its generation as a field, so the renewal follows with no lease read. A13 raised bytes_received by 1,333 with the same 55 calls: expiry seconds, the empty review-request lane and the RFC 3339 timestamps in every packet the two seats read.
